## Summary of Your Child Benefit Eligibility

Based on the official UK government guidance, here's your eligibility status for each child:

### ✅ **Alex - ELIGIBLE**
Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you can claim Child Benefit because you contribute £26.05 per week towards Alex's upkeep. This exceeds the Child Benefit payment amount, and importantly, no other claimant has priority over you.

### ✅ **Blake - ELIGIBLE**
Blake lives with you and meets all the standard eligibility criteria. You can claim Child Benefit for Blake as you're responsible for a child under 16 living in the UK.

### ❌ **Charlie - INELIGIBLE**
Unfortunately, you cannot claim Child Benefit for Charlie because someone who lives with Charlie is already claiming. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for the same child, and since another claimant is already receiving it, you are not eligible to claim for Charlie.

**Overall:** You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for **2 out of 3 children** (Alex and Blake). You should make your claim for these two children. Note that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

reasonings: Alex is 3 years old (under 16), not in care, hospital, or residential accommodation, and does not live with you. However, you are contributing £26.05/week towards Alex's upkeep. According to the guidance at gov.uk/child-benefit-child-lives-with-someone-else, you can continue to get Child Benefit for a child who doesn't live with you if you contribute to their upkeep by the same amount or more than the Child Benefit payment. The current Child Benefit rate for an eldest/only child is £25.60/week and for additional children is £16.95/week. Since you're contributing £26.05/week, this exceeds the Child Benefit amount, and importantly, no other claimant has priority. Therefore, you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.

Blake is 2 years old (under 16), lives with you, is not in care, hospital, or residential accommodation, is not fostered, does not work 24+ hours/week, has not started an apprenticeship, and does not receive qualifying benefits. According to gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and you live in the UK, and you'll usually be responsible if you live with them. Blake meets all the standard eligibility criteria. Therefore, you are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Blake.

Charlie is 3 years old (under 16), does not live with you, and someone who lives with Charlie is already claiming Child Benefit. According to gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. The guidance also states that if two people cannot agree who should claim, HMRC will decide, but in this case someone is already claiming. The guidance at gov.uk/child-benefit-child-lives-with-someone-else confirms that only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. Since someone else is already claiming Child Benefit for Charlie, you are INELIGIBLE to claim for this child.
